cards.title: Chemist uncle has a few requests
cards.body: He sees a crowd every day and remembers more than you think. Here's what makes his job, and your medicines, safer.

cards.title: Bring the prescription, every time
cards.body: Not "wahi wali goli". A prescription lets him give the right medicine at the right strength.

cards.title: Say who it's for
cards.body: Age, other medicines and health conditions all matter. "Kiske liye hai?" isn't nosiness. It's safety.

cards.title: Mention everything else they take
cards.body: Including medicines from other doctors. A chemist can catch clashes, but only if he knows the full list.

cards.title: Ask your questions
cards.body: How to take it, with food or without, what to do if a dose is missed. That's part of the job.

cards.title: Don't push without a prescription
cards.body: Some medicines legally need a prescription. When he says no, he's protecting you, not being difficult.

cards.title: Treat him as part of the team
cards.body: You probably see your chemist more often than your doctor. That makes him one of the most useful people in your parent's care.

takeaway: Bring the prescription, say who it's for, share other medicines and ask questions. Your chemist can help more than you think.
share: Send this to everyone who says "wahi wali de do" at the counter.
